name: Revispy Launchpad

sources.title: Homepage — review community platform: reviews, discussions, product/service catalogs, company profiles, Launchpad; 'Claim your company' flow for brands
Launchpad — weekly launch board (Week 39, Sep 21-27 2026 live) with upvote countdown and a 'Launch Now' button; catalog empty for anonymous viewers
Batch-provided create URL — returned 404; the live route is the 'Launch Now' button on /launchpad

conditions: Launching requires a Revispy account/profile — 'Create profile' (signup) precedes any launch
Whether the launch itself is free could not be confirmed behind the login wall — an /advertise page exists, so paid placement may be pushed
requirements: Product must fit the catalog model — products, services, companies are first-class entities on the platform
Weekly cadence: launches are ranked per UTC week with a voting window
preparation: Product name, URL, description, category, logo/screenshots
A Revispy profile (username claimed during signup)
Optionally claim/create the company profile so the launch attaches to a brand page
workflow: Sign up at https://www.revispy.com/signup and complete the reviewer/company profile
Fill the launch form and pick the launch week
Drive upvotes during the ~7-day voting window before rankings lock
watchFor: Very young platform — homepage hero claims '50K+ reviews' but the live counters render '0+'; treat marketing numbers as aspirational
The batch's /launchpad/create deep link 404s — enter through /launchpad → Launch Now
Catalog appears empty to logged-out visitors; actual community size is probably small
Advertise page exists — expect paid-promotion offers alongside the free launch
Several features (company analytics, AI insights) are marked 'coming soon' / preview-only
countsAsLive: The launch appears in the Launchpad catalog for its scheduled week with a public page others can upvote/discuss
unknowns: Whether launching is free or paid (flow gated behind login)
Exact form fields and any review/approval step
Actual user base — published counters suggest the platform is nearly empty
